title: DigitalHealth.London
funder: DigitalHealth.London (delivered by the Health Innovation Network (HIN) South London)
deadline_note: Applications are currently closed and no next cohort or date is published. The last round found on the official site was Cohort 8 (applications 8 May – 16 June 2024, programme started September 2024). No Cohort 9 announcement exists on digitalhealth.london as of 2026-11-24.

summary.at_a_glance: A twelve-month, NHS-delivered support programme for digital health SMEs whose product has usually already been piloted in the NHS and is ready to scale in London's health and care system. It gives no funding and takes no equity. Applications are closed and no future cohort has been announced.
summary.what_they_offer: Bespoke support over 12 months: an assigned NHS Navigator with NHS clinical or service-manager expertise, direct engagement with senior stakeholders, clinicians and healthcare experts, expert-led workshops and digital health advisors, and brokered connections to NHS organisations with specific challenges. The Accelerator 'can connect companies to relevant funding opportunities but does not provide or guarantee direct funding' and does not invest or take equity. Support is valued at an estimated £35,000 of Minimal Financial Assistance under the UK Subsidy Control Act 2022.
summary.what_theyre_looking_for: Per the official FAQs, at both application review and interview at least four professionals score applicants in three areas: (1) Credibility of business – financially viable, a working product, potential to succeed; (2) NHS and Social Care need and potential to help provide appropriate solutions – meeting a real demand (NHS Long Term Plan, NHSE Elective recovery strategy, Core20+5); (3) Potential to benefit from the programme – capacity to engage and reasonable expectations. Successful companies 'usually have a product or service that has already been piloted in the NHS and is ready to scale'; companies with capacity to fully engage 'have tended to have five employees or more'.
summary.who_can_apply: Eligibility criteria from the official FAQs: (1) must be an SME (fewer than 250 employees and turnover under €50 million or balance sheet total under €43 million); (2) 'registered with Companies House or equivalent' – charities and social enterprises are eligible; (3) committed to doing business in London, with a minimum of four mandatory face-to-face events in London during the year; (4) below the UK Minimal Financial Assistance threshold (£315,000 over three fiscal years; the programme counts as £35,000). NON-UK COMPANIES: 'International companies are eligible to apply ... but must be registered with UK Companies House and fit the requirements of an SME'; another FAQ says they 'must be registered with UK Companies House by the start of the programme and have a staff presence in the UK'. The Cohort 8 guidance says applicants without the registration must indicate their plans to register and submit evidence of completed registration by the start of the programme. Companies without a registered London address must demonstrate resources and commitment to work with London health and care organisations. No travel, visa or other costs are reimbursed. The Cohort 8 announcement said places go to 'up to 20 UK-registered businesses'. A US-only LLC with no UK Companies House registration, no UK staff and no NHS pilots would not meet these rules as written.
summary.how_to_apply: Based on the last (Cohort 8, 2024) round: (1) register for a SurveyMonkey Apply account on the 'Health Innovation Hub' application portal; (2) complete the online form – 4 question sections (Company Profile, Programme Eligibility, Policies in place, Application questions), 4 upload sections (Companies House registration and/or financial accounts, 60 second pitch video, other financial or regulatory information, company brochure/other material) and 2 sections to sign (Data Protection, Declaration); (3) applications are reviewed by health and care leaders and industry/commercial partners; (4) shortlisted applicants attend a virtual interview; (5) outcome announced, then an in-person onboarding day in Central London. No feedback is given at application-review stage; unsuccessful interviewees are offered a feedback call. Submitted applications cannot be edited.
summary.worth_noting: The official site shows no Accelerator cohort after Cohort 8 (17 companies, announced September 2024); the programme page (last modified 2026-08-24) and FAQs still say 'Applications to the Accelerator programme are currently closed' and point to the mailing list. The Accelerator is described as part-funded by the UK Shared Prosperity Fund. DigitalHealth.London's newest programme is the 10-week 'DigitalHealth.London Pathfinder' (Neighbourhood Health, 20 companies, open to a 'Registered company (UK or international) working or planning to work in London' with a product already deployed in a real-world health or care setting) – its applications are also closed and its first cohort runs 1 December 2026 – 19 February 2027. The Launchpad programme (earlier-stage companies) is also closed. Contact: info@digitalhealth.london.

portal.notes: For Cohort 8 the guidance says applicants must first register for a SurveyMonkey Apply login. The portal believed to be the one used (https://healthinnovationhub.smapply.io/ – its site title 'Health Innovation Hub' matches the screenshot in the official guidance, but the URL itself is not printed in any official document) currently shows 'Site Locked' with only an administrator login, so nothing can be started. In the 2024 form: sections can be saved and revisited ('save and continue editing') until marked complete; word limits show a countdown and a section over its limit cannot be submitted; the pitch video could be uploaded (MP4 or equivalent) or given as a URL; supporting evidence formats allowed were PDF, Word, Excel, Videos; once submitted the application cannot be amended. Other SM Apply sites show Google reCAPTCHA on account registration, but this could not be checked here because the site is locked.

questions_note: There is no live form: applications are closed and the SurveyMonkey Apply portal is locked. The list below is taken from DigitalHealth.London's own 'Accelerator Cohort 8 Applications: Application guidance' PDF (created 8 May 2024) – the most recent official guidance on the site; no newer cohort or guidance exists. It is therefore the 2024 form and may change if a new cohort opens. 'text' is the question/section heading exactly as printed in the guidance; 'help' is the guidance bullets for that heading (joined with ' | '), not necessarily the help text shown on the form itself. The guidance does not print the individual fields of sections 1 'Company Profile', 2 'Programme Eligibility' and 3 'Policies in place' (it only describes them: business/technology/sector profile, team skills, who will engage, funding and revenue; UK Companies House registration or plans to register, London resource and commitment, subsidy-control declaration; Net zero, EDI, Waste, founder background), so no fields are listed for those sections rather than inventing them. Field types are inferred (headings in section 4 are assumed to be free-text boxes); only the Elevator pitch word limit (100 words) is stated – other limits exist on the form ('Some sections have word limits which are clearly stated in the question') but are not given in the guidance. The guidance says 'All question sections are mandatory, but some document and media upload sections are optional'; sections 7 and 8 are stated as optional, the video is required (upload or URL), and whether the section 5 upload is mandatory is not stated. Spelling is kept as printed (e.g. 'NSH', 'here is they').
